provenance: 2026-07-20 optional-organ sweep, run after structural-dark row 5 closed. The sweep's structural result: of ~50 watchdog signal classes, exactly ONE watched for an available-but-UNADOPTED capability (aredn_organ_undeclared) -- 31 were liveness, 13 drift, 4 configured-but-broken. The domain is excellent at watching what it was told about and had almost nothing for what it was never told about. probe_lxmf_propagation_unused is the second such watcher: LXMF propagation nodes announce on the RNS network and the gateway ALREADY parses them into its own operator-owned node cache (measured: 14-15 heard within 6h on both gateway boxes) while gateway.json rns.propagation_node is empty. Consequence: an LXMF message to a peer that is offline right now fails outright, where a propagation node would hold it until the peer returns. Three traps this case guards: (1) treating the signal as a mechanical fix -- adoption is a TRUST decision, because a propagation node sees stored-traffic metadata, so standing one up on our own rnsd beats pointing at a stranger's, and the probe deliberately names the gap without prescribing a node; (2) reading a silent probe as 'propagation is fine' -- it is INERT wherever there is no gateway.json or no node cache, and a STALE cache HOLDS rather than claiming availability from dead bytes, so silence can mean unobservable; (3) using the journal as the evidence -- fleet boxes run Storage=volatile, so an absence of propagation log lines proves nothing, which is why the durable node cache is the source. Adoption edits gateway.json and needs a meshforge-gateway restart, which must never happen mid-soak (the wedge watchdog's os._exit(2) would activate new code non-deterministically).

provenance: 2026-07-20, slice 2 step 2c of the propagation leg. Context: MeshForge stood up its OWN LXMF propagation node (lxmd on moc1, hash 3968a2ee...) rather than adopt a stranger's, because a propagation node sees stored-traffic metadata. The moment gateway.json rns.propagation_node is set, the slice-1 detector probe_lxmf_propagation_unused goes INERT by design (one fault, one owner) -- so adoption shipped WITH probe_lxmf_propagation_node_dark, never before it. The plan states the rule bluntly: adopting alone trades a WATCHED gap for an UNWATCHED dependency, which is strictly worse than staying unadopted. Two legs with different fixes: STALE (the node is in the RNS node cache but has not announced for several announce periods -- it answered and stopped) and UNHEARD (the configured hash is absent from the cache entirely, which almost always means a wrong or truncated hash, i.e. the failure adoption itself introduces). The evidence is the durable operator-owned ~/.cache/meshforge/rns_nodes.json, never the journal, because fleet boxes run Storage=volatile and an absence of log lines proves nothing. The guard that makes the probe honest: it fires ONLY when some OTHER propagation announce reached the box within the window, which is positive proof the box can currently hear the propagation announce class -- so an RNS-wide transport wedge HOLDS as indeterminate and stays with its own owners (rns_rpc_unresponsive et al.) instead of being relabelled as this node's death. That is honest_failure_modes #2 applied to a liveness probe: unobservable is not dark. Detection is bounded below by several announce periods (~18h) because a propagation node announces every 360 min and a stranger's interval is not ours to know -- being late and right beats fast and wrong for a degraded capability signal.

Right after I set rns.propagation_node and restarted meshforge-gateway, the watchdog says the configured LXMF propagation node has NEVER been heard. Did I typo the hash? I also ran rnprobe lxmf.propagation and got 100% packet loss.

provenance: Live 2026-07-21: probe_lxmf_propagation_node_dark fired its UNHEARD leg minutes after the gateway restart that ADOPTION ITSELF REQUIRES, claiming the configured propagation node had NEVER been heard -- the wrong/truncated-hash fault it exists to catch. It was FALSE. Root cause was NOT the hash: node_models.to_dict() wrote service_type but node_tracker._load_cache() dropped it (honest_failure_modes #4, a writer with no reader), so every restart erased the RNS service type of every cached node until it announced again -- up to a propagation node's 360-min interval. The probe matches on service_type, so it was blind to a node the box had heard 7x in 25h and had delivered a store-and-forward message through 10 minutes earlier. Measured: 2 of 9,115 cached entries carried service_type, the oldest stamped AFTER the restart. TWO defects were needed, and the first fix alone did NOT cure it: (a) the loader dropped service_type, and (b) _merge_node() never refreshed service_* either, so an announce from an ALREADY-KNOWN node did not restore it. Verified live: after the next announce the cache entry had a fresh last_seen and service_type STILL None, and the probe kept firing. It was UNRECOVERABLE once lost, not self-healing -- the prediction 'it heals on the next announce' was wrong and was corrected the same day by the observation. Triage by the RESTART CLOCK, not by re-typing the hash: if the gateway restarted within ~6h and the node is otherwise alive (it announces, lxmd --status shows it serving, a drill delivers), it is this cache gap. Companion trap: rnprobe lxmf.propagation is NOT a delivery test -- it reports 100% loss against a healthy node, proven by a control from a box that had just completed a full round-trip through it.

2026-07-21, propagation arc slice 3. probe_lxmf_propagation_node_dark watches whether the configured LXMF propagation node ANNOUNCES; it cannot see whether that node STORES AND FORWARDS. A node announcing perfectly while silently dropping every stored message reads clean on it forever -- announce-liveness standing in as a proxy for the property actually depended on. The gap was structural in a 2-person lab: traffic to an OFFLINE peer essentially never happens organically, so the realistic failure was adopting the organ and having it be quietly useless for months with every gate green. The existing exerciser could not close it either -- lxmf_multi_user_synth builds every LXMessage with no desired_method, so all its traffic is DIRECT. Cure: an hourly drill that MANUFACTURES offline-peer traffic (a receiver that never announced, so no direct path can exist, is sent a PROPAGATED message and then pulls it back), consumed by probe_propagation_soak_degraded with an ENVELOPE leg (pass_envelope false) and a SILENCE leg (newest prop-*.json older than ~2.5 cadences -- for a fixed-cadence generator, going quiet IS the failure). The two probes are complementary and must not be conflated: node_dark firing means the node stopped announcing (or the configured hash is wrong); propagation_soak_degraded firing while node_dark is clean means the node is alive and announcing but is NOT doing its job. A STALE passing envelope must fire SILENCE, never read clean -- that is the exerciser-died-and-left-a-happy-file shape, mutation-pinned by test_propagation_soak_a_stale_PASS_still_fires_silence.

provenance: 2026-07-26 Row 8 cross_gateway_dups_unsuppressed ACCEPT ratified at frontier tier (operator decision 2026-07-19). The trap this case guards: an agent seeing a cross-gateway duplicate fire (or dual-homed recipient growth) and reflexively proposing a coordination/yield protocol. The invariant: an unsuppressed dup fails toward REDUNDANCY (arrives twice, visible); a coordination misfire fails toward SILENCE (arrives zero times, invisible) -- on emergency comms fail toward redundancy. On this fleet the dominant failure mode is PARTIAL failure (active-but-wedged, #68/#72), where a heartbeat-gated yield suppresses while the primary delivers nothing -- a heartbeat is a representation of delivery capability, not delivery. First lever on rising exposure is TOPOLOGY (single-home the recipient, or scope any yield to the RNS leg where confirms exist), never a general protocol. A human-class fire means investigate the instance in /fleet/dups fleet_duplicates[] and re-decide with it in hand; it does not auto-reopen the build. lore in .claude/research/cross_gateway_dup_design_inputs_2026_07_19.md
